tools.name: search_members
tools.description: Find people who can give the user a warm introduction or referral at a specific company, team, role, industry or city, for internships, new-grad jobs and career switches. Use this when someone asks how to get an internship or job at a company ("how do I get into Goldman Sachs", "can anyone refer me

tools.name: browse_directory
tools.description: Show the companies, roles and industries where the user can get a warm introduction or referral through Nepternship, with the people under each. Use this when someone wants to see where they could network into, asks which firms or industries they could get an internship or job referral at, or is sti

tools.name: get_member
tools.description: Return one member's full profile: who they can introduce the user to (role, company and details), what they are looking for themselves, industries, locations, university, and whether the user is already connected with them. Use this when the user wants to know more about a person from a search befor

tools.name: list_matches
tools.description: List the user's introductions: accepted ones with an open chat (including the free weekly curated match), requests waiting on the user, and requests the user sent that have not been answered yet. Use this for any question like "did anyone reply", "any new introductions", "is anything waiting on me"

tools.name: read_thread
tools.description: Return the messages in one introduction's chat. Use this when the user wants to read or catch up on a conversation with a matched member. Reading marks the messages as read for the user.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message in one of the user's active introductions (an accepted match). Use this only after the user has approved the exact text. Chat is free once an introduction is accepted; if a limit applies, the error explains it.

tools.name: request_balance
tools.description: Return how many introduction requests the user has left, any friend-referral credits, and their personal invite link. Use this when the user asks how many requests they have left, or after send_intro_request reports the limit.

tools.name: send_intro_request
tools.description: Send a Nepternship member an introduction request, with an optional note of up to 200 characters, for the person they can introduce the user to (for example an analyst at JPMorgan or an engineer at Google). Use this when the user wants an intro or referral from a member returned by search_members, b

tools.name: respond_to_request
tools.description: Accept or decline an introduction request that is waiting on the user (status pending in list_matches). Accepting opens a chat with the other member. Declining is private; the requester is not notified and requests expire on their own after 30 days. Confirm with the user before declining.

tools.name: get_upgrade_link
tools.description: Return the user's Nepternship Premium checkout link (on nepternship.com) with their price and trial length, or their manage-subscription link if they already subscribe. Use this only when the user explicitly asks to upgrade or asks how to get more intro requests after hitting the free limit.

tools.name: signup_peek
tools.description: Given what a prospective member is looking for, return example companies, roles and industries where members can make introductions, with sample offerings and first names. Use this while a new member is joining, right after they say what they are looking for.

tools.name: sign_up
tools.description: Save a new member's answers to the Nepternship join questions: what they are looking for (up to 3 industries, a preferred location and a sentence about the opportunity), whether their university career center referred them, their name, university and graduation year, and who they can introduce other

tools.name: connect_account
tools.description: Connect the user's Nepternship account to this assistant through Nepternship's sign-in page (Google, Apple or email, plus a verified mobile number for new members). Use this when an existing member wants to see their introductions or asks to sign in, or when a new member has saved their join answers

tools.name: get_my_profile
tools.description: Return the signed-in user's own Nepternship profile: name, university, what they are looking for, who they can introduce others to, industries, preferred locations, and introduction requests remaining. Use this when the user asks about their own profile or settings.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "send_intro_request" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "sign_up" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_members, list_matches, read_thread · Private data: respond_to_request, sign_up · Public sink: send_message, send_intro_request, sign_up, connect_account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_members, list_matches, read_thread · Private data: respond_to_request, sign_up · Public sink: send_message, send_intro_request, sign_up, connect_account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
